text.p: Warship manufacturer Vosper Thornycroft Holdings Plc said on Thursday that it was confident in the profitability of its order book and believes 1997/98 will be another successful year for the company.
"Prospects for further growth thereafter continue to depend on winning further work for both the core and developing businesses," chairman Lord Wakeham said in the results statement.
The group reported an 11 percent jump in pre-tax profits for the year to March 31, 1997 to 30.7 million stg and a final dividend of 26 pence per share, also up 11 percent.
It said that around 40 percent of the group's turnover now arises from activities independent of warship contracts.
"Sold financial performance has come from a good overall order book and a considerably broadened business base," Lord Wakeham said.
An order book of 300 million stg includes the seven-ship Royal Navy minehunter contract but excludes 140 million stg worth of work won by the Flagship Training and Vosper-ManTech joint ventures.
The group said it made "considerable progress" in the past year on its ship programmes.

Customer acceptances have been received for the final Saudi minehunter, a second Oman corvette and the first two Qatari first strike craft. A third Qatari vessel has been accepted in the new financial year.

A Memorandum of Understanding has also been put in place with Qatar for a British Defence package which includes two patrol craft. The company said detailed technical and support discussions are now at an advanced stage.
